title: Subject–Verb Agreement
intro: Subject–verb agreement requires that a finite verb agree with its real grammatical subject in number (singular/plural) and person (1st/2nd/3rd). The key to WBPSC questions is ignoring intervening prepositional modifiers and identifying the true grammatical head.
bengali:
Subject এবং Verb-এর মধ্যে বচন (Number) ও পুরুষ (Person)-এর সামঞ্জস্য বজায় রাখাই হলো Subject-Verb Agreement। বাক্যের আসল Subject-কে চেনা জরুরি, কারণ Subject ও Verb-এর মাঝের অতিরিক্ত শব্দগুচ্ছ (prepositional phrase) কখনোই Verb-কে প্রভাবিত করে না।

WBPSC পরীক্ষায় সবচেয়ে বেশি আসা নিয়মসমূহ:
১. Proximity Trap: Subject ও Verb-এর মাঝে 'of', 'in', 'with' ইত্যাদি থাকলে শেষ শব্দটি দেখে Verb ঠিক করবেন না। যেমন: 'The quality of these mangoes is good' (এখানে Subject হলো 'quality', তাই 'is' হবে; 'mangoes'-এর জন্য 'are' হবে না)।
২. 'As well as', 'along with', 'together with': দুটি Subject যুক্ত হলে Verb সর্বদা প্রথম Subject অনুযায়ী হয়। যেমন: 'The teacher, as well as the students, was present.'
৩. 'Either...or', 'Neither...nor': এক্ষেত্রে Verb সর্বদা নিকটবর্তী Subject (দ্বিতীয় Subject) অনুযায়ী হয়।
৪. 'Each', 'Every', 'Neither of', 'Either of': এগুলির পরে Noun প্লুরাল হলেও Verb সর্বদা SINGULAR হয়। যেমন: 'Neither of the boys was present.'
৫. 'A number of' (Plural verb) বনাম 'The number of' (Singular verb)।

rules.rule: Intervening prepositional phrases do not affect the verb: The head subject alone controls the verb number.
examples: The quality of these apples is exceptional (Subject = 'quality', singular).
A bouquet of red roses was presented to the chief guest.
The causes of this widespread disease are being investigated.
exceptions: Fractions, percentages, and expressions of quantity ('most of', 'some of', 'half of') take singular verbs with uncountable nouns and plural verbs with countable plural nouns.

rules.rule: When two subjects are joined by 'as well as', 'along with', 'together with', 'in addition to', 'accompanied by', 'like', 'unlike', the verb agrees strictly with the FIRST SUBJECT.
examples: The captain, along with his crew members, was awarded medals.
The players, as well as the head coach, were felicitated by the governor.
I, like my brother, am interested in civil services.
exceptions: Never look at the second subject near the verb when these connectors are present.

rules.rule: When subjects are joined by 'either...or', 'neither...nor', or 'not only...but also', the verb agrees with the NEAREST subject (proximity rule).
examples: Neither the principal nor the teachers were present in the staff room.
Neither the teachers nor the principal was present in the staff room.
Not only the clerk but also the officers have agreed to the revised terms.
exceptions: In interrogative questions, the verb agrees with the subject immediately following it: 'Was neither the manager nor his assistants informed?'

rules.rule: 'Each', 'Every', 'Everyone', 'Somebody', 'Nobody', 'Either of', 'Neither of' take a strictly SINGULAR verb.
examples: Each of the candidates has submitted his certificate.
Neither of the two roads leads to the railway station.
Everyone in the auditorium was astonished by the presentation.
exceptions: When 'each' appears directly AFTER a plural subject, it takes a plural verb: 'The boys each have a distinct duty'.

rules.rule: 'A number of + plural noun' takes a PLURAL verb; 'The number of + plural noun' takes a SINGULAR verb.
examples: A number of applicants have appeared for the screening test (denotes 'many').
The number of candidates appearing is twenty-five thousand (denotes a single statistical figure).
exceptions: 'A number' = Many (Plural verb); 'The number' = A fixed count (Singular verb).

rules.rule: 'More than one + singular noun' takes a SINGULAR verb; 'More than two/three' or 'More + plural noun + than one' takes a PLURAL verb.
examples: More than one employee was dismissed for misconduct.
More employees than one were dismissed for misconduct.
More than two persons were eyewitnesses to the accident.
exceptions: Pay close attention to noun word order: 'More than one candidate was' vs 'More candidates than one were'.

rules.rule: 'Many a + singular noun' takes a SINGULAR verb and singular possessive pronoun; 'A great many + plural noun' takes a PLURAL verb.
examples: Many a soldier has laid down his life for the nation.
A great many tourists have visited Darjeeling this season.
exceptions: Do not be confused by the word 'Many' in 'Many a'—the noun following 'a' is singular, so the verb must be singular.

rules.rule: Nouns denoting fixed sums of money, periods of time, weights, or distances regarded as a single unified unit take a SINGULAR verb.
examples: Ten miles is a substantial distance to walk on foot.
Fifty thousand rupees is the total admission fee.
Five years is a sufficient tenure for executing this urban project.
exceptions: When the amount or units are distributed, spent individually, or divided among entities, use a plural verb: 'Fifty thousand rupees were distributed among the victims'.

rules.rule: Collective nouns (committee, jury, team, council, family, crew) take a SINGULAR verb when acting as a unit, but a PLURAL verb when members act individually or disagree.
examples: The jury has delivered its unanimous verdict (acting as one unit).
The jury are divided in their opinions (members in disagreement).
The committee has approved the budgetary proposal.
exceptions: In WBPSC, check pronouns: 'its' signals singular verb, while 'their' signals plural verb.

rules.rule: Nouns that are plural in form but singular in meaning (Mathematics, Physics, Politics, News, Innings, Measles, Rickets) take a SINGULAR verb.
examples: Mathematics is an engaging subject for analytical minds.
The news from the border was reassuring.
Politics is his chosen sphere of public activity.
exceptions: When preceded by a possessive pronoun or 'the' denoting practical abilities or views, words like 'mathematics' or 'politics' take plural verbs: 'His mathematics are weak'.

commonMistakes: Writing 'Neither of the two books are useful' instead of 'Neither of the two books is useful' (Neither takes singular verb).
Writing 'The teacher as well as the students were felicitated' instead of 'The teacher as well as the students was felicitated' (as well as agrees with Subject 1).
Using a plural verb after 'The quality of the products are...' instead of 'The quality... is...' (head noun controls verb).
Writing 'A number of students was absent' instead of 'A number of students were absent' (A number takes plural).
Writing 'Many a men have failed' instead of 'Many a man has failed' (Many a takes singular noun and singular verb).
examTricks: The Preposition Filter: Cross out everything between 'of' and the verb to find the real subject.
'As well as / Along with' Formula: Verb = Subject 1.
'A number of' = PLURAL; 'The number of' = SINGULAR.
memoryTricks: FIRST for As-well-as; NEAREST for Neither-nor.
A number are MANY; THE number is ONE.
revision: Head subject controls the verb; ignore 'of + noun'.
As well as / along with / together with -> agrees with Subject 1.
Either...or / neither...nor -> agrees with nearest subject.
Each, every, everyone, neither of, either of -> Singular verb.
A number of + plural verb; The number of + singular verb.
Many a + singular noun + singular verb.
Ten miles is (distance as a unit); Fifty thousand rupees is (sum as a unit).
